title: SIEVES: Selective Prediction Generalizes through Visual Evidence Scoring
abstract: arXiv:2604.25855v3 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: As the accuracy of Multimodal large language models (MLLMs) on traditional visual question answering benchmarks approaches saturation, reliable deployment requires satisfying low error tolerances in real-world out-of-distribution (OOD) scenarios. Selective prediction aims to improve coverage, i.e. the share of inputs the system answers, while adhering to a user-defined risk level. This is typically achieved by assigning a confidence score to each answer and abstaining on those that fall below a certain threshold. Existing selective prediction methods rely on text-only reasoning and learn to predict confidences simply based on whether the answer was correct or not. In contrast, we introduce SIEVES (Selective Prediction through Visual Evidence Scoring), which first requires the answering model to provide visual evidence supporting its answer, by returning crops of the image alongside their textual reasoning and answer. translated_abstract: 随着多模态大语言模型（MLLMs）在传统视觉问答基准上的准确率接近饱和，可靠部署需要在现实世界的分布外（OOD）场景中满足低错误容忍度要求。选择性预测旨在提高覆盖率（即系统所回答输入的比例），同时遵守用户自定义的风险水平。这通常通过为每个答案分配置信度分数，并对低于特定阈值的答案进行弃答来实现。现有的选择性预测方法仅依赖纯文本推理，并仅仅根据答案是否正确来学习预测置信度。与之相反，我们提出了SIEVES（通过视觉证据评分实现选择性预测），该方法首先要求答题模型提供支持其答案的视觉证据，即在返回文本推理和答案的同时返回图像的裁剪区域；其次，一个（原文摘要在此处截断）
tldr: 该论文提出SIEVES方法，通过要求模型提供图像裁剪作为视觉证据并对其进行评分来估计置信度，从而提升多模态大语言模型选择性预测在分布外场景中的泛化能力。
en_tdlr: SIEVES improves the generalization of selective prediction for MLLMs in out-of-distribution scenarios by requiring answering models to provide visual evidence (image crops) that is scored to estimate confidence.
